en: (서울=연합뉴스) 장진리 기자 = JTBC가 중국 산둥방송국과 손잡고 한중 미디어 콘텐츠 교류 확대에 나선다고 26일 밝혔다. 양사는 지난달 말 다큐멘터리 공동 제작을 위한 양해각서(MOU)를 체결하고 한중 양국의 역사와 문화를 아우르는 콘텐츠 제작을 본격적으로 추진하기로 했다. 첫 프로젝트는 짜장면을 소재로 한 다큐멘터리다. 100여년 간 이어진 한중 양국의 식문화 교류 역사를 조명하며, 내년 초 양사의 TV와 온라인동영상서비스(OTT) 플랫폼을 통해 공개한다. 후속 작품도 논의 중이다. 산둥방송국은 지난 12일 JTBC에 한국과 중국의 인연이 있는 도시들을 소개하는 콘텐츠 '두 도시 이야기'의 공동 제작도 제안했다. 양사는 내년 중 방송을 목표로 제작 방향과 방영 일정 등을 협의하고 있다. 산둥방송국은 중국 산둥성 정부 산하의 주요 방송 미디어 기관으로, 8개 라디오 주파수와 9개 TV 채널을 비롯해 온라인 및 모바일 플랫폼을 운영한다. 한중 자유무역협정(FTA) 서비스·투자 후속 협상을 계기로 양국의 문화 콘텐츠 교류 확대에 대한 기대가 커지는 가운데 이번 협력이 이뤄진 점이 의미 있다고 JTBC는 설명했다. JTBC는 "산둥방송국과의 협력을 계기로 중국 주요 방송사들과 파트너십을 확대하고, 콘텐츠 공동 제작과 현지 유통은 물론 문화·관광 분야의 다양한 사업 기회도 발굴해 나갈 계획"이라고 말했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/26 09:51 송고 2026년11월26일 09시51분 송고

The discussions, believed to have lasted more than a week, were the second round of such talks in the Arunachal Pradesh sector since September. They were held following reports of aggressive posturing by Chinese troops along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), especially in the Upper Subansiri region. “A meeting of the senior, highest military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently. Discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management, as also addressing outstanding issues along the LAC,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing when he was asked about the talks. “Such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and preventing any escalation,” he said. India and China regularly engage through diplomatic and military mechanisms, he added. Lt Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Indian Army’s 3 Corps based near Dimapur in Nagaland, led the Indian side at the talks held in the second week of November, while the Chinese side was headed by his counterpart. In September, Kalia and a Chinese military commander held flag talks in two sessions on either side of the LAC in the Arunachal Pradesh sector. Tensions erupted between the Indian Army and the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) at Taksing, a remote area of Upper Subansiri district, in July and August. The Indian side said at the time that the two sides had agreed to use diplomatic and military mechanisms to “avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation” along the border. A similar mechanism for talks between military commanders already exists in the western sector, which includes Ladakh, the scene of a military face-off in 2020 that dragged on for more than four years and took bilateral relations to a six-decade low. The Indian side has maintained that the state of the border will determine the overall course of the relationship with China. During the military and diplomatic talks, India has stressed to the Chinese side the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas for the continued development of bilateral ties. The two sides have taken a series of measures to rebuild their ties since October 2024, when they reached an understanding on disengaging frontline forces at several “friction points” along the LAC in the Ladakh sector. At the same time, the Indian side has bolstered military preparedness and infrastructure along the LAC in the Arunachal Pradesh sector. At a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the margins of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September, Prime Minister Narendra Modi stressed that both sides must show sensitivity to each other’s core issues and that bilateral relations should be guided by the “three mutuals” – mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest. Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer

A senior North Korean official has held talks with China's top envoy to Pyongyang and reiterated her country's commitment to cementing relations with Beijing, the Chinese Embassy in the North said Tuesday. Ryu Un-hae, vice minister at the Ministry of External Economic Relations, met Chinese Ambassador Wang Yajun at the embassy in Pyongyang on Monday, taking stock of progress in bilateral ties following the summits between North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September 2025 and again in June, according to the embassy. Ryu said that under the "strategic" guidance of the two countries' leaders, bilateral relations have entered a "new phase," while pointing to "positive progress" in bilateral cooperation in various fields, according to the embassy. "North Korea's Ministry of External Economic Relations is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with relevant departments, such as the Chinese Embassy and China's Ministry of Commerce, to contribute greatly to pushing for the development of North Korea-China relations," Ryu was quoted as saying. He also reaffirmed Beijing's "firm" and "unwavering" position about maintaining and solidifying its traditional relations with Pyongyang. "The Chinese Embassy is willing to work with the Ministry of External Economic Relations to better implement important agreements reached by the top leaders of the countries and further deepen practical cooperation in the economy, trade and other fields to benefit the people of both nations," the ambassador was quoted as saying. Relations between North Korea and China have recently improved following high-level exchanges and reciprocal visits by the two countries' leaders. In July, Ryu accompanied North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song during Pak's trip to China to attend events marking the 65th anniversary of the signing of the North Korea-China Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance
